_comment: policy.verify_command:
The completion gate. Until this was set, nothing checked that the suite was green
before work was marked done — the gate existed but was disarmed, so 'done' rested on
the agent's own account of it. On PR #96 that produced a task reported complete
against a tree that failed CI.
`make verify` is the right command because it is already what CONTRIBUTING points at
and it needs no cluster, cloud or database credentials: build, the full unit suite,
golangci-lint, the SPDX header policy and the manifest gates. Integration and E2E are
deliberately NOT in it — they need `make infra-up`, so a machine without Docker
Compose could never satisfy the gate and the pressure would be to disable it.
Green here is necessary, not sufficient: it says nothing about whether the tests
assert anything. Mutation-check before reporting done regardless.
TDD gate exemptions — plain glob strings.
web/admin/app/**/layout.tsx:
Next.js route segment config (`export const dynamic`) and layout composition are
declarative build-time conventions with no runtime behaviour a unit test can
observe. A test here would assert that a constant equals itself.
NOTE: this exemption originally rested on two reasons, the second being that
web/admin had no test runner at all. That reason is gone — vitest now runs via
`pnpm --filter @hermes/admin test`, wired into ci-web.yml. The first reason stands
on its own, so the exemption stays; it is no longer a placeholder for missing
infrastructure.
TESTED BY: `next build` in .github/workflows/ci-web.yml. The entire effect of
`dynamic = "force-dynamic"` is on the build — without it the build tries to
prerender authenticated pages and fails. The build is the assertion, and it now
runs in CI.
sdks/typescript/packages/*/src/types.ts:
Type-only declaration modules: `export type` / `export interface` aliases over the
OpenAPI-generated schemas, plus the client config interface. They emit no runtime
JavaScript at all, so there is no behaviour for a test to observe — importing one
at runtime yields an empty module.
TESTED BY: `tsc --noEmit` via the `typecheck` script, run for every SDK package in
.github/workflows/ci-web.yml. Because tests are included in tsconfig.json (and
excluded only from tsconfig.build.json), every fixture in every suite is checked
against these types — that is what turned the group_id -> category_id rename into a
compile error instead of a green suite pinned to a field nobody has. The generated
schemas underneath are additionally guarded by .github/workflows/sdk-drift.yml.
sdks/typescript/packages/*/src/index.ts, .../src/testing/index.ts:
Barrel files. Every line is a re-export; the modules behind them carry the
behaviour and their own suites.
TESTED BY: the suites of the modules re-exported, plus `tsc --noEmit`, plus the
cross-package build in ci-web.yml — hermes-web and hermes-react resolve
hermes-client's types through its built dist/, so a symbol missing from a barrel
fails their typecheck.
examples/demo-server/src/main.ts:
Process entry point, and nothing else: read env vars, construct the SDK client, call
createHandler, listen. It calls process.exit on missing config and binds a socket, so
there is no seam a unit test can hold — and deliberately so. Every piece with
behaviour was extracted specifically to be testable: routing and the identity rule in
server.ts, token assembly in session.ts, cookie signing in cookies.ts, the two proxy
rules in proxy.ts, and the node<->WHATWG conversion in http-adapter.ts. Between them
those carry ~70 tests.
TESTED BY: tests/browser (Playwright), which boots this exact file as a `webServer`
entry and drives the real widget against a real cluster through it — so a broken wiring
line fails every browser spec. Run by `make demo-e2e` and nightly in
.github/workflows/e2e-live.yml. Additionally `pnpm --filter @hermes/demo-server build`
typechecks it in ci-web.yml.
examples/react-demo/src/**/*.tsx, examples/react-demo/vite.config.ts:
The demo's host-application chrome and its build config. These are the *subject* of the
browser suite rather than something a unit test should pin: their whole purpose is to be
a realistic page with the widget embedded in a header, and the properties worth asserting
(a notification arrives over the real socket with no refetch, the badge is exact, actions
round-trip to the real API, ::part restyling works) are only observable in a real browser
against a real cluster. A jsdom test of this JSX would assert that a div contains a div.
The extractable logic was deliberately pulled out and IS unit-tested: token-refresh
scheduling in src/session.ts, which cannot be tested by waiting because the admin API
refuses an expires_in below 3600 seconds.
TESTED BY: tests/browser/tests/*.spec.ts — smoke, realtime-arrival, unread-count,
inbox-actions, pagination, theming, session-refresh and multi-user-isolation all drive
this app. Run by `make demo-e2e` and nightly in .github/workflows/e2e-live.yml.
ci-web.yml additionally runs a real `vite build` plus `tsc --noEmit` over these files.
